name: Schema-Dependent Encoding Pathways
short_description: Prior knowledge (schemas) determines encoding pathway: schema-congruent → rapid vmPFC-mediated cortical integration; schema-incongruent → strong hippocampal PE encoding; schema-irrelevant → weak encoding on both
higher_order_principle: Prior knowledge (schemas) fundamentally alter the encoding pathway. Schema-congruent information is rapidly integrated via vmPFC-mediated neocortical pathway with reduced hippocampal involvement. Schema-incongruent information triggers strong hippocampal encoding via PE. Schema-irrelevant information is poorly encoded by both pathways. This three-way split means that the same instructional method has different effects depending on what the learner already knows.

neural_substrate.vmPFC_role: detects match between new input and existing neocortical schema

causal_links.evidence_base: van Kesteren et al., 2012; Tse et al., 2007; Tse et al., 2011

parameters.congruent: vmPFC facilitates rapid neocortical integration (bypasses hippocampus)
parameters.incongruent: vmPFC detects mismatch → signals hippocampus for strong PE-driven encoding
parameters.irrelevant: no schema activated → neither pathway strongly engaged

parameters.speed: fast — can integrate within a single exposure
parameters.memory_quality: gist-like, semantic (knows the fact but may not remember learning episode)
parameters.instructional_implication: lecture and direct instruction CAN work for schema-congruent material

causal_links.evidence_base: van Kesteren et al., 2012; Greve et al., 2017

parameters.PE_strength: HIGH — violation of existing schema produces large PE
parameters.memory_quality: detailed, episodic (remembers surprising information AND context of learning)
parameters.instructional_implication: MUST first activate the incorrect schema, THEN present correcting information. Conceptual change pedagogy: 'predict → test → confront → resolve.'
MUST provide scaffolding — organizational framework, advance organizer (Ausubel), or analogy — BEFORE presenting details. Create the schema first.

scope_conditions: Schemas are individual — each learner has different prior knowledge
Schema strength modulates: strong schemas produce stronger congruence/incongruence effects
vmPFC is the SAME node identified in architectural neuroscience as domain-general regulatory hub
Cultural and domain knowledge differences affect schema activation
moderators: instruction_sequence (activating schema before vs after presenting material)

interactions.nature: ED4's schema detection determines which encoding pathway (ED1) is activated.
Schema incongruence is a high-level prediction error that engages the same PE mechanisms as T1.

ecological_testability: HIGH — prior knowledge assessable by pretest; encoding pathway inferable from memory quality (gist vs. detail); schema congruence manipulable by instructional design.

key_references.citation: van Kesteren, M. T. R., Ruiter, D. J., Fernández, G., & Henson, R. N. (2012). How schema and novelty augment memory formation. Trends in Neurosciences, 35(4), 211–219.
Tse, D., Langston, R. F., Kakeyama, M., et al. (2007). Schemas and memory consolidation. Science, 316(5821), 76–82.
Tse, D., Takeuchi, T., Kakeyama, M., et al. (2011). Schema-dependent gene activation and memory encoding in neocortex. Science, 333(6044), 891–895.

Greve, A., Cooper, E., Tibon, R., & Henson, R. N. (2017). Knowledge is power: Prior knowledge aids memory for both congruent and incongruent information. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 148(2), 325–341.
